Problem description:
There is a set of candidate facilities, each with a fixed opening cost,

Decision variables:
- Decide which facilities to open.
- Assign each customer to exactly one opened facility.

Constraints:
- Each customer must be assigned to exactly one opened facility.
- Assignments can only be made to facilities that are opened.
- There are no capacity constraints on facilities.

Objective:
Minimize the total cost, defined as the sum of facility opening costs and customer-to-facility connection costs.

{{INSTANCE_INPUT}}

Return your decision in **exactly** this JSON format:
```json
{
  "solution": {
    "selected": [<location_to_open>, <location_to_open>, ...],
    "assignments": [<chosen_open_location>, <chosen_open_location>, ...]
  }
}
```
**Do not include explanations or any extra keys.**

contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.

City planning staff should decide which neighborhood libraries to open and allocate every regular reader to a single opened branch to minimize the combined cost of opening libraries and reader travel, and readers may use only branches that are opened.

As a festival organizer, choose which kitchens to activate for event catering and assign every order to a single activated kitchen so the total of kitchen activation fees and delivery distance is kept minimal, with orders fulfilled only by kitchens that are activated.

I need you to pick which electric vehicle chargers to install in our complex and register every resident's car to a single installed charger to keep the sum of installation charges and walking distance as small as possible, and cars can only be linked to chargers that are installed.

Our farmers market manager should decide which pop up clothing stalls to rent and allocate every shopper to a single rented stall to minimize stall rental outlay plus shopper travel, with shoppers visiting only stalls that are rented.

My neighborhood association wants to choose which community tool sheds to maintain and sign up every household with a single maintained shed to minimize the total of maintenance expenses and households' travel burden, and households may access only sheds that are maintained.

As the owner of a pet grooming service, decide which mobile vans to deploy around town and schedule every appointment with a single deployed van so that deployment costs and travel are minimized, and appointments may only be assigned to vans that are deployed.

Our grocery chain must pick which pickup hubs to open and register every customer to a single opened hub to minimize the sum of hub opening charges and customer travel costs, ensuring customers are served only by hubs that are opened.

As a community garden coordinator, choose which plots to prepare and assign every interested family to a single prepared garden to keep the combination of setup expenses and family travel as low as possible, and families may only be assigned to gardens that are prepared.

The tutoring program manager should decide which weekend centers to launch and enroll every student at a single launched center to minimize the total of center launch costs and student commuting, with students attending only centers that are launched.

I am asking you to choose which bike repair kiosks to install along the trail and route every rider to a single installed kiosk so the combined installation expense and detour distance are minimized, and riders may use only kiosks that are installed.

Our disaster relief team needs to pick which emergency supply caches to stock and assign each household to a single stocked cache to minimize stocking costs plus retrieval distance, with households allowed to use only caches that are stocked.

As the festival vendor coordinator, decide which artisan stalls to rent and place every vendor at a single rented stall to minimize total stall rent and customer walking distance, with vendors occupying only stalls that are rented.

The office manager should choose which remote work pods to set up in the campus and allocate each freelancer to a single set up pod to minimize pod setup charges combined with commuter inconvenience, and freelancers may use only pods that are set up.

As the school district administrator, decide which temporary classroom trailers to bring in and assign every after school student to a single brought trailer to minimize trailer bringing costs plus student travel time, and students attend only trailers that are brought in.

My waste management group wants to choose which recycling drop off points to maintain and link each block to a single maintained point to minimize maintenance outlay and carrying distance, with blocks using only points that are maintained.

As a farm market operator, decide which roadside produce stands to operate this season and direct each regular customer to a single operating stand so the overall cost of running stands and customer travel is minimized, and customers visit only stands that are operating.

The community music director should choose which piano practice rooms to keep available and assign each musician to a single available room to minimize room upkeep plus musician walking time, and musicians may practice only in rooms that are available.

As a charity coordinator, pick which satellite donation boxes to place around the city and assign every donor to a single placed box to minimize placement fees combined with donor detour effort, ensuring donors use only boxes that are placed.

Our social services office needs to determine which evening soup kitchens to fund and direct every nearby person in need to a single funded kitchen so that funding commitments plus travel are as low as possible, and people may be routed only to kitchens that receive funding.

As the building IT lead, choose which small servers to power up around the floor and bind every connected device to a single powered server to minimize the total of powering costs and latency penalties, and devices may connect only to servers that are powered up.

I run a mobile charging service and need you to pick which charging stations to activate and link every user to a single active station, minimizing the combined activation charges and user detour expenses.

As a school administrator planning afternoon tutoring sites, choose which rooms to offer and allocate every student to a single offered room so the sum of room rental costs and student travel inconvenience is kept as low as possible.
For a community library outreach, pick which bookmobile stops to operate and assign each patron to a single active stop to minimize the aggregate cost of operating stops and patron distance.
I organize a farmers market network and need to select which distribution points to run and route every vendor to a single running point, minimizing total setup charges plus vendor hauling costs.

As the event planner for a city festival, decide which information booths to staff and direct each attendee to a single staffed booth so the total staffing expenses and visitor walking burdens are minimized.
Running a small courier startup, choose which parcel depots to open and bind every delivery to a single open depot in order to minimize depot opening spending plus delivery connection costs.

For a neighborhood tool library, determine which lending lockers to put in service and register each borrower to a single serviced locker so the sum of locker installation costs and borrower retrieval effort is minimized.

As a public health coordinator, pick which vaccination sites to operate and assign each resident to a single operated site to keep the total cost of running sites and resident travel as low as possible.

I manage a fleet of mobile pet groomers and need to choose which grooming tents to set up and allocate each client to a single set up tent to minimize overall tent setup fees plus client travel or pickup cost.

As a city planner for waste collection, decide which dropoff locations to maintain and map each household to a single maintained location to minimize the combined maintenance costs and household travel burden.

For a tech company offering edge servers, choose which server nodes to enable and route every user to a single enabled node so the total of node activation expenses and user latency costs is minimized.

I run a neighborhood meal pickup program and must choose which kitchens to open and assign each recipient to a single open kitchen to minimize the overall kitchen opening costs plus meal delivery or pickup cost.

As a pop up retail coordinator, pick which booths to open and link each customer group to a single open booth so the total of booth rental fees and customer travel or service costs is as small as possible.
For a bike share operator, decide which docking stations to commission and register every rider to a single commissioned station to minimize commissioning expenses plus rider access inconvenience.
I organize community tutoring and need to choose which volunteer hubs to activate and assign each learner to a single active hub so the combined volunteer hub costs and learner travel are minimized.

As a disaster relief coordinator, select which supply depots to open and allocate each affected household to a single open depot to minimize the sum of depot opening costs and household pickup effort.

Running an art rental service, decide which pickup points to make available and appoint each client to a single available point so that the total of point operation fees and client connection costs is minimized.
For a local meal kit delivery service, choose which packing centers to operate and assign every order to a single operating center to minimize center opening charges plus order shipping cost.

I manage a community shuttle network and must pick which shuttle stops to bring online and assign each commuter to a single online stop so the total of stop activation expenses and commuter travel cost is minimized.

Help our cafe chain manager pick which neighborhood outlets to open and link each block to exactly one open outlet to minimize the total of outlet setup charges plus the delivery and customer travel cost.
As the event organizer, choose which food truck spots to staff and direct each attendee area to exactly one staffed spot so the sum of stall rental fees and attendees' walking distances is minimized.

Assist the hospital logistics lead in selecting which cold storage depots to operate and direct each clinic to exactly one active depot, keeping the total of depot operating charges and per clinic transport expense as small as possible.

As the retailer’s distribution planner, decide which micro warehouses to activate and assign every shop to exactly one active hub to minimize the aggregate of hub opening fees and shipment costs to shops.

As the school district administrator, choose which book lending branches to open and register each neighborhood school with exactly one open branch to keep the sum of branch opening costs and delivery or pickup costs as low as possible.

As a food bank director, pick which distribution points to operate and match each community group to exactly one operating point, minimizing the total of running fees and volunteer or transport costs.

Help a mobile clinic coordinator decide which pop up health posts to staff and assign every residential cluster to exactly one staffed post so the overall cost of staffing those posts plus patient travel remains minimal.

As a regional farmer cooperative manager, select which central pickup sites to maintain and attach each local farm to exactly one maintained site to minimize the sum of site maintenance expenses and farmers' delivery costs.

Assist a ridesharing company in picking which charging hubs to enable and map each vehicle parking zone to exactly one enabled hub so the combined cost of enabling hubs and drivers' repositioning is as small as possible.

As a nonprofit organizer, determine which clothing distribution centers to open and allocate every shelter to exactly one open center in order to minimize the sum of center opening expenses and transportation costs.

Help a municipal planner choose which public lockers to install and assign each commuter catchment to exactly one installed locker to keep the total of installation fees and commuter detour costs as low as possible.

As an office supply chain manager, choose which print shops to contract and link every department to exactly one contracted shop so that the total of contract fees plus per department delivery expense is minimized.

Assist a pet adoption network in selecting which foster hubs to fund and pair each applicant region with exactly one funded hub so the aggregate of hub funding and adoption transfer costs is as small as possible.
As a community gardening coordinator, decide which tool sheds to build and assign each garden plot to exactly one built shed, minimizing the total of construction costs and gardeners' hauling effort.

As a recycling program manager, select which processing points to activate and enroll each neighborhood in exactly one active point so the sum of activation fees and household dropoff costs is minimized.

Assist a tutoring network in choosing which learning centers to open and register each student cluster with exactly one open center to keep the total of center opening costs plus students' travel or remote connection expense as low as possible.

facility_item_fields.name: facility_id
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a candidate pop-up health post (used to refer to this post when deciding whether to staff it and when assigning clusters).

facility_item_fields.name: opening_cost
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: The staffing cost to open (staff) this particular pop-up health post; added to total cost if the coordinator staffs this post.

connection_item_fields.name: facility_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the pop-up health post being considered as the destination for a residential cluster (matches post_id in facility items).

connection_item_fields.name: customer_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a residential cluster (a group of patients) that must be assigned to exactly one staffed post.

connection_item_fields.name: cost
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Connection cost representing the travel cost (e.g., distance, time, or inconvenience) for the residents of the given cluster to use the specified post.

global_fields.name: num_facilities
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate central pickup sites (potential sites the co-op can choose to keep running). Used to know how many site records exist.

global_fields.name: num_customers
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of local farms that must be attached to exactly one maintained pickup site.

global_fields.name: opening_costs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list (or array) of maintenance/upkeep costs for each candidate pickup site. If a site is kept active, its corresponding cost is paid once.

facility_item_fields.name: facility_id
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) for a candidate pickup site used to reference that site in decisions and cost entries.

facility_item_fields.name: opening_cost
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: The maintenance/upkeep cost for this specific pickup site; included in total cost only if the site is chosen to remain active.

connection_item_fields.name: facility_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the pickup site referenced by this connection cost entry (matches a site_id from facility items).

connection_item_fields.name: customer_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the local farm/customer that must be assigned to a maintained pickup site.

connection_item_fields.name: cost
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: The delivery/travel cost for the specified farm to use the specified pickup site (e.g., distance-based or transport expense); this cost applies if the farm is assigned to that site.

global_fields.name: num_facilities
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate charging hubs the company may enable. This is the count of distinct hub locations considered for opening.

global_fields.name: num_customers
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of parking zones (vehicle pools) that must each be assigned to exactly one enabled hub.

global_fields.name: opening_costs
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of enabling fees (one per candidate hub) the company must pay to enable that charging hub. The list order corresponds to the facility identifiers used elsewhere.

facility_item_fields.name: facility_id
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a candidate charging hub (e.g., an index or code). Used to refer to this hub when deciding whether to enable it and when assigning parking zones.

facility_item_fields.name: opening_cost
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to enable this particular charging hub. If the hub is opened in the solution, this fee is paid once regardless of how many zones are assigned to it.

connection_item_fields.name: facility_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the candidate charging hub involved in this connection cost entry; matches the hub_id used in facility items.

connection_item_fields.name: customer_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the parking zone whose vehicles would be sent to the specified hub if assigned here.

connection_item_fields.name: cost
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: The cost (e.g., driver time + fuel, in monetary units) to move vehicles from the given parking zone to the specified hub. This cost applies for each zone assigned to that hub and contributes to the total connection cost.

global_fields.name: num_facilities
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate clothing distribution centers being considered for opening in the town; an integer count used to index the list of centers.

global_fields.name: num_customers
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of shelters that must receive clothing; an integer count used to index the list of shelters that each must be assigned to exactly one open center.

global_fields.name: opening_costs
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list or array of monetary costs to activate each candidate distribution center (one cost per center); include the same ordering/indexing as used for center identifiers.

facility_item_fields.name: facility_id
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific candidate clothing distribution center (used to reference this center when deciding whether to open it and when assigning shelters).

facility_item_fields.name: opening_cost
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to open this particular distribution center; if the center is opened this cost contributes to the total objective.

connection_item_fields.name: facility_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the distribution center from which a shelter would be served (matches the center_id used in facility entries).

connection_item_fields.name: customer_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the shelter (customer) that must be assigned to exactly one open distribution center.

connection_item_fields.name: cost
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: The transportation cost (monetary) incurred if this shelter is served from this distribution center; used along with opening costs to evaluate total solution cost.

global_fields.name: num_facilities
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate public locker locations under consideration for installation.

global_fields.name: num_customers
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of commuter catchment areas (neighborhood groups) that must each be assigned to exactly one installed locker.

global_fields.name: opening_costs
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of installation fees for each candidate locker location (one fee per locker), representing the cost to install that locker.

facility_item_fields.name: facility_id
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier for a specific candidate locker location; used to reference that locker when deciding whether to install it and which catchments may use it.

facility_item_fields.name: opening_cost
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary fee to install this particular locker location (the planner pays this if the locker is chosen).

connection_item_fields.name: facility_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the locker location being considered as a service point for a catchment (matches a locker_id from facility items).

connection_item_fields.name: customer_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a commuter catchment area (which must be assigned to exactly one installed locker).

connection_item_fields.name: cost
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: The detour cost incurred by commuters in that catchment if they are assigned to this locker (e.g., extra travel time or distance); used together with installation fees to compute total cost.

global_fields.name: num_facilities
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate print shops you may choose to contract for office printing and delivery.

global_fields.name: num_customers
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of departments in the office that each must be assigned to exactly one contracted print shop.

global_fields.name: opening_costs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of contract fees for all candidate print shops; you pay a shop's fee if you decide to contract that shop.

facility_item_fields.name: facility_id
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a candidate print shop used to reference it when selecting contracts and assigning departments.

facility_item_fields.name: opening_cost
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: The contract fee for this specific print shop; included in the total cost if this shop is contracted.

connection_item_fields.name: facility_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the print shop offering delivery to a department (links to the print_shop_id above).

connection_item_fields.name: customer_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a department that must be assigned to one contracted print shop.

connection_item_fields.name: cost
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: The delivery (per-department) cost when this print shop supplies and delivers to the specified department; added to the total when the department is assigned here.

global_fields.name: num_facilities
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate foster hubs under consideration for funding; the count of distinct hub options the network may choose from.

global_fields.name: num_customers
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of applicant regions (areas with adopters) that must each be assigned to exactly one funded foster hub.

global_fields.name: opening_costs
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of the funding amounts required to open each candidate foster hub; if a hub is selected, its corresponding funding cost is added to the total expense.

facility_item_fields.name: facility_id
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific candidate foster hub; used to reference this hub when deciding to fund it and when assigning applicant regions.

facility_item_fields.name: opening_cost
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: The funding amount required to open this particular foster hub; paid once if the hub is chosen.

connection_item_fields.name: facility_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the candidate foster hub involved in this connection record, matching the hub_id used in facility items.

connection_item_fields.name: customer_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for an applicant region that must be assigned to a funded hub.

connection_item_fields.name: cost
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to transfer a pet from the given applicant region to the specified foster hub; incurred if that region is assigned to that hub.

global_fields.name: num_facilities
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of proposed tool-shed sites in the neighborhood that could be built.

global_fields.name: num_customers
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of garden plots that each need to be assigned to exactly one built shed.

global_fields.name: opening_costs
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of construction costs for each proposed shed site; paying this cost opens (builds) that shed for use by plots.

facility_item_fields.name: facility_id
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific proposed tool-shed site (used to reference that site elsewhere).

facility_item_fields.name: opening_cost
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to build the specific shed at this site; if chosen, this cost is added to the total plan cost.

connection_item_fields.name: facility_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the shed site from which hauling effort to a plot is measured (links a hauling cost to a specific shed).

connection_item_fields.name: customer_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a garden plot that must be assigned to exactly one built shed.

connection_item_fields.name: cost
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: The hauling effort or travel cost for gardeners if the given plot is served by the given shed (added to total when that assignment is made).

global_fields.name: num_facilities
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate recycling processing points available to potentially activate in the program.

global_fields.name: num_customers
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of neighborhoods that must each be enrolled with exactly one active processing point.

global_fields.name: opening_costs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of activation fees for all candidate processing points (one fee per processing point), contributing to the total cost if that point is opened.

facility_item_fields.name: facility_id
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a candidate processing point (used to reference that point when deciding whether to activate it and when assigning neighborhoods).

facility_item_fields.name: opening_cost
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary fee required to activate this specific processing point; counted once if the point is opened.

connection_item_fields.name: facility_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the processing point offering dropoff service — matches the processing_point_id used in facility items to link connection costs to that point.

connection_item_fields.name: customer_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a neighborhood that must be assigned to exactly one active processing point.

connection_item_fields.name: cost
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Cost for households in the given neighborhood to drop off recyclables at the specified processing point (incurred per neighborhood assignment).

global_fields.name: num_facilities
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate learning centers (venues) the tutoring network may choose to open.

global_fields.name: num_customers
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of student clusters (groups of students) that must each be assigned to exactly one opened learning center.

global_fields.name: opening_costs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of opening fees for each candidate learning center; if a center is opened its corresponding fee is added to the total cost.

facility_item_fields.name: facility_id
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a candidate learning center (used to reference this center in opening costs and connection-cost entries).

facility_item_fields.name: opening_cost
facility_item_fields.scenario_description: Up‑front cost to open this specific learning center; incurred once if the center is chosen to be opened.

connection_item_fields.name: facility_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the learning center for this connection entry (links a student cluster to a specific center).

connection_item_fields.name: customer_id
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the student cluster that must be assigned to exactly one opened learning center.

connection_item_fields.name: cost
connection_item_fields.scenario_description: Cost to serve the given student cluster from the given learning center (travel time/cost, remote connection expense, or similar per-cluster service cost).
